﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ [This is a Book] meaning: this is a Book ﴿which We have sent down to you﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿to bring mankind out of darkness into light﴾, meaning: to call them from the darkness of misguidance to the light of faith.[[See: al-Tabari 16/511-512.]]

It is said: by the knowledge of their Lord.[[Abu Ja'far al-Tabari said in his Tafsir (16/512): "The Exalted has attributed the bringing forth of people from darkness into light to His Prophet (ﷺ) by the permission of their Lord granted to them for that, for he is the guide of His creation and the one who grants success to whomever of them He loves for faith, since it was from him that their summoning to it came, and his informing them of what is theirs and what is upon them in it. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 2–3:

﴿Allāhi alladhī﴾ Abū Ja'far and Ibn ʿĀmir read "Allāhu" with a nominative (raf') vowel, as a new sentence (isti'nāf), with its predicate (khabar) following. The rest read it with a genitive (khafḍ) vowel, as an adjective (naʿt) of "al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd" [[See: al-Ṭabarī: 16/512–513.]]. Yaʿqūb, when he connected the words, would read it with a genitive vowel.

Abū ʿAmr said: the genitive is by inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr). Its meaning is: "To the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy," [[Al-Ṭabarī said (16/513–514): "The scholars of Arabic have differed in its interpretation when it is read thus. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he would read it with the genitive and say: its meaning is: 'By the permission of their Lord, to the path of (Allah), the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs what is in the heavens.' He said: it is from the postponed (mu'akhkhar) which means the advanced (muqaddam), and he illustrates it with the saying of a speaker: 'I passed by the elegant ʿAbd Allāh,' and a phrase that is placed in the position of the noun as an adjective, then the noun is placed in the position of the adjective, so that its case-inflection follows the inflection of the adjective which was placed in the position of the noun, as some poet said: 'If you were possessed of a spear and a sharp-bladed sword, I would not fear the attacks of the wicked wolf.' As for al-Kisāʾī, he said, as is reported from him: whoever reads with the genitive intends to make it one sentence, and he made the genitive follow the genitive, and it was with the genitive that he would recite." Then he said: "The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings; both have been recited by imams of the readers, their meaning is one, and whichever one the reader recites is correct. It is possible that the one who recited with the nominative intended the meaning of the one who recited with the genitive, in following one part of the speech with another, but he used the nominative because it is separated from the verse before it, as the Exalted said: 'Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties' to the end of the verse, then He said: 'The repentant, the worshippers' (Surah al-Tawbah: 111–112)."]] ﴿alladhī lahu mā fi l-samāwāti wa-mā fi l-arḍ, wa-wayl lil-kāfirīna min ʿadhābin shadīd﴾ [[Al-Ṭabarī said (16/514): The meaning of His words "Allah, the One to whom belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth" is: Allah, who possesses all that is in the heavens and on the earth. He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): We have sent down to you this Book so that you may call My servants to worship One with such attributes, and to abandon worship of gods and idols who possess for themselves and for others neither harm nor benefit. Then the Exalted threatened those who disbelieved in Him and did not respond to the call of His Messenger to what he called them to, namely the sincere monotheism toward Him, saying: "And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment," meaning: the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell, for whoever denies His oneness and worships others along with Him, from the severe punishment of Allah.]].

﴿alladhīna yastaḥibbūna﴾ — they prefer (yakhtārūna), ﴿al-ḥayāta l-dunyā ʿala l-ākhira wa-yaṣuddūna ʿan sabīli llāh﴾ — that is, they prevent people from accepting the religion of Allah, ﴿wa-yabghūnahā ʿiwajan﴾ — that is, they seek it crooked and inclined; it means: they seek the way of Allah while deviating from the right course.

It was also said: the pronoun (hā') refers to the world (al-dunyā), meaning: they seek the world by a path of deviation from the truth, that is, toward what is unlawful (ḥarām).

﴿ulāʾika fī ḍalālin baʿīd﴾ [[That is: these disbelievers who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter are in far-off departure from the truth, and taken by other than guidance, and deviating from the direct path. See: Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 16/515.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 4–5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make [the message] clear to them﴾, in their language, so that they may understand from him.

If it is said: How is this so, when the Prophet ﷺ was sent to all of creation?

It is said: He was sent from among the Arabs, in their language, and the rest of people follow them. Then the messengers were dispatched to the outlying regions, calling them to Allah, mighty and majestic, and translating for them in their own tongues. [[Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Arzi raised this question at length and answered it from several angles. The first: the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in one language is sufficient, because translation for the people of the other languages makes up for its being revealed in all languages, and brevity suffices, as is the case in the Mighty Qur'an. The second: its being revealed in one language is further from distortion and alteration, and safer from dispute and disagreement. The third: if it had been revealed in the languages of the people, and were miraculous in each one of them, and the Arab Messenger spoke to each nation in its own language just as he spoke to his own community to which he belonged, that would have been close to compulsion and coercion, rather than enabling free choice. So, since its being revealed in one language was sufficient, the most appropriate of the languages was the language of the Messenger's people, because they were closest to him and most able to understand him. See: Masa'il al-Razi wa-ajwibatuha min gharib ayat al-tanzil by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Razi al-Hanafi, pp. (157–158).]].

﴿So Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

﴿And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs, [saying]: "Bring your people out of the darknesses into the light"﴾, that is: from disbelief to faith through the call. ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mujahid and Qatadah said: "the blessings of Allah." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/520–523; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/6.]] Muqatil said: "the events of Allah among the earlier nations." It is said: "So-and-so is knowledgeable of the Days of the Arabs," meaning their battles. What is intended is what occurred in the Days of Allah of blessing and trial, and the mention of "days" suffices for them, because these were known to them. [[al-Tabari transmitted this view and the evidence the proponents cited for it. Ibn Atiyyah said in al-Muharrar al-Wajiz (8/203): "The word 'days' encompasses both meanings, because reminding occurs through both aspects together."]].

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful﴾. "Sabbar" means one who is very patient, and "shakur" means one who is very grateful. He intended: for every believer, because patience and gratitude are among the characteristics of the believers.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 14, verses 6–7:

﴿And when Moses said to his people: "Remember God's blessing upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord."﴾ [[Al-Tabari related from Ibn 'Uyayna in its interpretation, he said: "God's favours (ayadi) upon you and His days (ayyam)."]] Al-Farra' said: The cause that brings this waw (conjunction) is that God Most High informed them that the people of Pharaoh tormented them with kinds of torment other than slaughter, and with slaughter. Since He dropped the waw in "yudhabbihuna" (they slaughter) and "yuqattiluna" (they kill), He intended to explain the torment with which they subjected them. [[Al-Tabari added further clarification, saying in his Tafsir (16/524): "The waw was inserted in this place because by His words 'they slaughter your sons' He intended to report that the people of Pharaoh tormented the Children of Israel with kinds of torment other than slaughter, and with slaughter. In another place in the Qur'an it came without the waw: 'they subject you to terrible torment, they slaughter your sons' [al-Baqara: 49] in one place, and in another: 'they kill your sons' [al-A'raf: 141]. The waw was not inserted in the places where it was not inserted, because by His words 'they slaughter' and 'they kill' He intended to specify the attributes of the torment with which they subjected them. The same applies to every clause whose elaboration is intended: without the waw it is an elaboration; and when it is intended to join it to something else, which is neither the elaboration nor its like, the waw is used." For a more detailed treatment, consult Abu Ja'far Ibn Ibrahim Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnati in his book "Mulak al-Ta'wil," edited by Dr. Mahmud Kamil Ahmad: 1/53–57.]] ﴿and they spare your women﴾: they leave them alive. ﴿In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾: God says: in what the people of Pharaoh did to you of kinds of torment, there was a tremendous trial from your Lord, i.e., a test and an examination for you from your Lord. [[The word "balaʾ" (trial) in this place may mean a blessing (ni'ma), and it may also mean the affliction that befalls people through hardships.]] See Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/525.

﴿And when your Lord declared﴾: i.e., made known. It is said: "adhdhana" and "ta'adhdhana" have the same meaning, like "awʿada" and "tawaʿʿada" (both meaning to threaten). ﴿If you give thanks﴾ for My blessing by believing and obeying ﴿I will surely increase you﴾ in blessing.

It was said: Thanks is the binding of what exists and the hunting of what is lost.

It was said: "If you give thanks" by obedience, "I will surely increase you" in reward.

﴿But if you deny﴾ My blessing, rejecting it and not giving thanks for it, ﴿indeed My punishment is severe﴾. [[Al-Tabari said (16/528): "And His words, 'But if you deny…' mean: and if you deny, O people, the blessing of God, rejecting it by not giving thanks for it and by opposing His command and prohibition, and committing His acts of disobedience, then 'indeed My punishment is severe': I will punish you as I punished whoever among My creatures denied Me."]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verse 8–9:

﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth altogether, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾ That is: Free of need of His creation. Ḥamīd (Praiseworthy): praised in His actions, because in them He is bountiful and just.

﴿Has there not come to you the report of those﴾ — the news of those — ﴿before you: the people of Noah, ʿAad, Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows except Allah.﴾ That is: whoever came after the people of Noah, ʿAad and Thamud.

It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited this verse and then said: "The genealogists have lied" (kadhaba al-nassābūn) [Narrated by al-Ṭabarī: 16/529 and 530; al-Suyūṭī added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. See: al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/9.]

And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Between Ibrahim and ʿAdnan there are thirty generations (qarn), whom none knows except Allah the Exalted." [It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "Between the time of Moses and the time of Noah there were thirty generations (qurūn), whom none knows except Allah." It is also transmitted from him by al-Mahdawī that he said: "Between ʿAdnan and Ismaʿīl there were thirty fathers who are not known." Ibn ʿAṭiyyah, after citing these two reports in al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz: 8/206, said: "Fixing their number is far-fetched, and negating knowledge of them altogether is more sound, and it is the wording of the Qur'an." Ibn al-Jawzī in Zād al-Masīr (2/348) related from Ibn al-Anbārī, in explaining the verse, that he said: "That is: none can count their number except Him; moreover, Allah destroyed many nations among the Arabs and others, so their reports ceased and their traces were effaced, and none knows them except Allah." See also: Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/344, 345.]

Mālik ibn Anas used to dislike that a person should trace his own lineage back to Adam as a father, and likewise regarding the Prophet ﷺ, because none knows those forefathers except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Their messengers came to them with the clear proofs﴾ — with the evident signs — ﴿but they put their hands into their mouths.⁠﴾ Ibn Masʿūd said: they bit their hands in rage [Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Firyābī, Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Ḥākim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak. al-Haythamī said: "al-Ṭabarānī narrated it from his shaykh ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, who is weak." See: al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/10; Zād al-Masīr: 4/348; Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 7/43.] as He said: ﴿They bite their fingertips at you in rage⁠﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 119].

Ibn ʿAbbās said: When they heard the Book of Allah, they marvelled and returned their hands to their mouths. [See: Zād al-Masīr: 4/349; al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 5/408.]

Mujāhid and Qatādah said: They denied the messengers and rejected what they brought. It is said: "I returned so-and-so's words into his mouth," meaning I denied him. Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 14, verse 17:

﴿Yatajarra'uhu﴾ means he sips it and drinks it, not in one gulp but mouthful by mouthful, because of its bitterness and heat. ﴿Wa-la yakadu yusighuhu﴾: "yakadu" is a *sillah* (a grammatically redundant particle), so the meaning is "he does not swallow it," as in His saying, ﴿lam yakad yarahā﴾ [al-Nur: 40], meaning "he did not see it."

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "He does not let it pass down."

It was also said: the meaning is "he almost does not swallow it, and when he does swallow it, it boils in his belly."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawba told us; Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us; Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud told us; Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal told us; 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Busr, from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying, ﴿and he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips⦆ [Ibrahim: 16–17]. He said: "It is brought near to his mouth and he hates it; when it is brought closer to him, it scorches his face and the skin of his head falls off. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it comes out from his anus." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scorches the faces﴾ [al-Kahf: 29].

[Narrated by al-Tabari in *al-Tafsir* (*tafsir*: his exegesis of the Qur'an), 16/549–550; and al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on the description of Hell, the section on what has been related about the drink of the people of the Fire, 7/303–304, and he said: "This is a *gharib* hadith. Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) said it from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Busr, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Busr is not known except in this hadith." It was also narrated by al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak*, 2/351, who said: "This is a *sahih* hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Imam Ahmad narrated it in *al-Musnad*, 5/265, and the author (al-Baghawi) in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 15/243–244. Al-Albani graded it weak in his commentary on *Mishkat al-Masabih*, 3/1581.]

As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and death comes to him from every place﴾, it means that he feels the anguish and pain of death from every part of his body.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: "Even from beneath every hair of his body."

It was also said: death comes to him from in front of him and behind him, from above him and below him, and from his right and his left.

﴿And he is not dead﴾, so that he might find rest. Ibn Jurayj said: his soul is suspended at his throat, so it does not leave his mouth and he dies, and it does not return to its place in his body so that life benefits him. ﴿And behind him﴾, meaning before him, ﴿is a severe punishment﴾, meaning a harsh one. It was also said: the severe punishment is eternal abiding in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verse 18:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes⁠—﴾ meaning: the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened﴾ [al-Zumar: 60], that is: you will see the faces of those who lied about Allah blackened. ﴿Like ashes on which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾: He described the day as stormy, but stormy is a attribute of the wind, since the wind occurs in it, just as it is said: "a hot day" and "a cold day," because the heat and the cold are in it.

It has also been said: its meaning is "on a day of stormy wind," and the "wind" was omitted because it had been mentioned before. This is a parable which Allah struck for the deeds of the disbelievers, meaning: they will not benefit from their deeds which they did in the world, because they associated others with Allah in them, like ashes which the wind has scattered, from which no benefit is gained. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They have no power over anything they have earned﴾, meaning: the disbelievers, ﴿of what they earned﴾ in the world, ﴿over anything﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the far-reaching error.﴾ (193/a)

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 19–21:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "خالقُ السمواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ" (khaliqu as-samawati wal-ard, "Creator of the heavens and the earth"), and in Surat an-Nur "خَالِقُ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ" (khaliqu kulli dabbah, "Creator of every creature"), in the annexed form (idafah, a grammatical construction linking two nouns).

The others read "خَلَقَ" (khalaqa, "created") in the past tense, with "وَالْأَرْضِ" (wal-ard) and both in the accusative (naSb).

"بِالْحَقِّ" (bil-haqq, "with truth") means: He did not create them in vain, but created them for a great purpose. ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾, others who would be more obedient to Allah than you.

﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾, meaning not hard to overcome, mighty. It means that things are easy for His power; nothing is difficult for Allah the Exalted, however great and immense it may be.

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they will come out before Allah all together﴾ [i.e., they will come out of their graves to Allah and appear, all together] [[The text between the brackets is omitted from "b".]] ﴿Then the weak will say﴾, meaning the followers, ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾, i.e., who acted with pride toward people, and they are the leaders and chiefs: ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, plural of tabi' (follower), like haras and haris (guard and guards), ﴿so will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾ Mughnun means "repelling," ﴿from us any of the punishment of Allah?﴾.

﴿They will say﴾, meaning the leaders who were followed: ﴿If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you﴾, i.e., if Allah had guided us, we would have called you to guidance. But since He led us astray, we called you to misguidance [[In "a": al-dalal.]], ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or are patient; for us there is no place of escape﴾, meaning no refuge and no deliverance.

Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire, "Come, let us show anxiety," and they will show anxiety for five hundred years, but the anxiety will not benefit them. Then they will say, "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for five hundred years, but it will not benefit them. Then they will say: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or are patient; for us there is no place of escape﴾ [[Al-Tabarani narrated it from Ka'b ibn Malik as a marfu' report, and Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also recorded it, and in its chain is Anas ibn al-Qasim. Ibn Abi Hatim said: he is unknown (majhul). See: Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/43, al-Durr al-Manthur 5/17, al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 2/288.]].

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 5/18, Tafsir al-Tabari 16/564.]] said: It has reached me that the people of the Fire cried out to the guardians. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment"﴾ [Ghafir: 49]. The guardians responded to them: "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They said, "Yes." The guardians responded to them: ﴿Call, but the call of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [Ghafir: 50]. When they despaired of what was with the guardians, they called out: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 77]. They asked for death, but it was not granted them for eighty years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is like a thousand years of what you count. Then after the eighty years He glanced at them and said: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾. When they despaired of what had come before, some of them said to others: "Calamity has descended upon you, as you see. So come, let us be patient; perhaps patience will benefit us, as the people of the world were patient in obedience to Allah and it benefited them." They agreed to be patient. Their patience lasted long, then they grew anxious and called out: "It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or are patient; for us there is no place of escape," i.e., no means of deliverance.

He said: At that point Iblis stood up and addressed them, saying: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth," and so on to the end of the verse. When they heard his words, they loathed themselves, and it was called out to them: ﴿The hatred of Allah toward you is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were being called to faith but disbelieved﴾ [Ghafir: 10]. They said, and they called out a second time: "Return us, and we will do righteousness; indeed, we are certain." He answered them: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, and the verses that follow [al-Sajdah: 12–13]. They called out a third time: ﴿Our Lord, delay us to a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers﴾ [Ibrahim: 44]. He answered them: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no decline?﴾, and the verses that follow [Ibrahim: 44]. Then they called out a fourth time: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do﴾. He answered them: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? And the warner came to you﴾, the verse [Fatir: 37]. He said: He remained with them for as long as Allah willed. Then He called to them: "Were My verses not recited to you, and did you not deny them?" When they heard that, they said: "Now He will have mercy on us." Then they said at that point: "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return, then we are wrongdoers." He said at that point: ﴿Be silent therein and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 105–108]. At that, hope and supplication were cut off from them. Then some of them turned upon others, gnawing at each other's faces, and the Fire closed over them.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verse 22:**

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Satan will say﴾, meaning Iblis, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning it has been concluded, so the people of Paradise have been admitted to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

Muqatil said: A pulpit (minbar) is placed for him in the Fire, and he climbs it. The disbelievers gather around him, blaming him, and he says to them:

﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth﴾, so He fulfilled it for you. ﴿And I promised you, but I failed you.﴾ It was also said: he says to them, "I told you there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire."

﴿And I had no authority over you﴾, meaning no power. It was also said: I did not bring you any proof regarding what I invited you to. ﴿Except that I invited you﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: "but rather, I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves" for answering me and following me without any authority or proof. ﴿I cannot help you﴾, meaning cannot give you relief, ﴿nor can you help me﴾, meaning give me relief.

Al-A'mash and Hamzah read "bi-musrikhiyy" with a kasra on the ya' (yā'), while the others read it with a fatha because of gemination (tadh'if, doubling of the consonant). Whoever read it with a kasra did so because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn), so the letter was given a kasra, since the ya' is a sister of the kasra. The grammarians did not approve of this reading. It was also said that it is the dialect of the Banu Yarbu'. The original form was "bi-musrikhiyni-ya", the nun was dropped because of the idafa (genitive construction), and the ya' of the plural was assimilated into the ya' of the possessive suffix.

﴿Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with me before﴾, meaning: I disbelieve in your making me a partner in His worship, and I disassociate myself from that.

﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿will have a painful punishment.﴾

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah informed us; Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harith informed us; Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us; Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us; Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal narrated to us; Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad informed me, from Dukhayn al-Hajari, from Uqbah ibn Amir (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding the hadith of intercession. He mentioned the hadith, then said: "Jesus (peace be upon him) will say, 'Go to that unlettered Prophet.' So they will come to me, and Allah will permit me to stand. I will rise from my gathering with the best fragrance anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will grant me intercession and make for me a light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot. Then the disbelievers will say, 'The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so who will intercede for us?' They will say, 'None but Iblis, for he is the one who misled us.' So they will come to him and say, 'The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so stand up and intercede for us, for you are the one who misled us.' He will stand up and rise from his gathering with the foulest smell anyone has ever smelled, and then Jahannam will be made to groan (yu'azzamu) [[In "b": "yu'azzimu li-Jahannam" as also in al-Tabari. In the Bulaq edition of it: "yu'azzimu nahibahum" (their wailing is magnified). Shaykh Shakir said: this is other than what the manuscript, al-Durr al-Manthur, and Ibn Kathir agree upon... I am in doubt about the word, and my opinion is: "yuqattamu li-Jahannam," from the saying "qattama al-sharib," when a drinker tastes a drink and dislikes it, shrinks, and frowns.]]. At that moment he will say: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth﴾ up to the end of the verse."

[[Narrated by al-Darimi in al-Raqa'iq, chapter on intercession: 2/327, and by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 16/562-563. al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir, and said: "They narrated it with a weak chain." Al-Haythami said: al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, who is weak. Shaykh Mahmud Shakir said: this report is weak and cannot stand. Rishdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri is weak and abandoned (matruk), and has disconnected (ma'adil) and unusual (munkar) reports. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/18, Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/376, al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/18, Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/530.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 23–24:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ Some of them greet one another, and the angels greet them.

It is also said: the one who greets with peace is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example?﴾ "Have you not considered" means "Have you not known." A mathal (parable) is a saying that circulates to liken one thing to another.

﴿A good word﴾ and it is the saying "There is no god but Allah." ﴿Like a good tree﴾ and it is the palm tree, meaning like a tree of good fruit. [[This is what al-Tabari preferred in his Tafsir (16/573), because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the trees there is one whose leaf does not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is." People began thinking of the trees of the desert. Abdullah said: "It came into my mind that it is the palm tree, but I felt shy. Then they said: Tell us what it is, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "It is the palm tree." Related by al-Bukhari in Knowledge, chapter on the narrator's saying "haddathana and akhbarana" (1/145), and in Sales, and in Tafsir, and in other places; and by Muslim in the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter "The Likeness of the Believer is the Likeness of the Palm Tree," no. (2811) (4/2164–2165); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/307).]]

And Zabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: it is a tree in Paradise. [[In "B": al-Sham.]]

﴿Its root is firm﴾ in the earth, ﴿and its branches﴾ its top, ﴿are in the sky.﴾ Likewise, the root of this word is firmly established in the heart of the believer through knowledge and affirmation; when he speaks it, it ascends, and it is not blocked until it reaches Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up﴾ [Fatir: 10].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 23–24:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ Some of them greet one another, and the angels greet them.

It is also said: the one who greets with peace is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example?﴾ "Have you not considered" means "Have you not known." A mathal (parable) is a saying that circulates to liken one thing to another.

﴿A good word﴾ and it is the saying "There is no god but Allah." ﴿Like a good tree﴾ and it is the palm tree, meaning like a tree of good fruit. [[This is what al-Tabari preferred in his Tafsir (16/573), because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the trees there is one whose leaf does not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is." People began thinking of the trees of the desert. Abdullah said: "It came into my mind that it is the palm tree, but I felt shy. Then they said: Tell us what it is, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "It is the palm tree." Related by al-Bukhari in Knowledge, chapter on the narrator's saying "haddathana and akhbarana" (1/145), and in Sales, and in Tafsir, and in other places; and by Muslim in the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter "The Likeness of the Believer is the Likeness of the Palm Tree," no. (2811) (4/2164–2165); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/307).]]

And Zabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: it is a tree in Paradise. [[In "B": al-Sham.]]

﴿Its root is firm﴾ in the earth, ﴿and its branches﴾ its top, ﴿are in the sky.﴾ Likewise, the root of this word is firmly established in the heart of the believer through knowledge and affirmation; when he speaks it, it ascends, and it is not blocked until it reaches Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up﴾ [Fatir: 10].

﴿تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا﴾ tu'ti ukulaha: "it gives its fruit," ﴿كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا﴾ "every season, by the permission of its Lord." Al-hin (الْحِينُ) in the language means "time."

They differed over its meaning here. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: al-hin here means a full year, because the palm tree bears fruit every year.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and al-Hasan said: six months, from the time its spathe (ito'laha, إِطْلَاعِهَا) appears until its harvesting (siramiha, صِرَامِهَا). This was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

It was also said: four months, from the time it appears until it ripens.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: two months, from the time it is eaten until the time of harvesting.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "every season" means every morning and evening, because the fruit of the palm is eaten at all times, by night and by day, in summer and in winter, whether as dates (tamr), fresh dates (ruṭab), or half-ripe dates (busr). Likewise, the deed of the believer rises at the beginning of the day and its end, and the blessing of his faith never ceases; rather, it reaches him at every time.

[[See these five opinions on the meaning of "al-hin," and a sixth opinion from 'Ali that it means eight months, in: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/575-579; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/24-25; Zad al-Masir: 4/359; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/422. Al-Tabari said: "The most correct of these opinions in my view is the view of the one who said that by al-hin in this place is meant: morning, evening, and every hour; because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, made the fruit that this tree gives at every season a parable for the deed and speech of the believer. There is no doubt that the believer has raised up to Allah, every day, good deeds and words, not only every year, or every six months, or every two months. If that is so, there is no doubt that the parable cannot contradict what it illustrates in meaning; and if that is so, the soundness of what we have said becomes clear. If someone says: 'Which palm tree gives its fruit at every time, eaten in summer and in winter?' It is said: in winter, the spathe is eaten from it; and in summer, the unripe dates (balah), the half-ripe dates (busr), the fresh dates (ruṭab) and the dried dates (tamr), all of which are from its fruit."]].

As for the wisdom in likening faith to a tree: a tree is not a tree except by three things: a firmly rooted root, a standing trunk, and a high branch. Likewise, faith is not complete except by three things: assent in the heart (taṣdiq), speech with the tongue (qawl), and action with the body ('amal).

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tayasfuni informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani informed us: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated to us that he heard Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among trees there is a tree whose leaf does not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is." 'Abd Allah said: People thought of the trees of the desert, and it came to my mind that it was the palm tree, but I felt shy. Then they said: "Tell us what it is, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "It is the palm tree." 'Abd Allah said: I mentioned that to 'Umar, and he said: "For you to have said it is the palm tree would have been dearer to me than such and such."

[[Agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh), and its takhrij was mentioned shortly before, p. (346), footnote. [[In "B": "its head" (ra's-aha).]]]]

It was also said: the wisdom in comparing it with the palm tree among all other trees is that the palm tree is the most like a human among trees, in that if its head is cut off, it dries up, whereas other trees branch out from their sides after their heads are cut off. (3) And because it resembles a human in that it bears fruit only through pollination (al-talqih). And because it was created from the surplus of the clay of Adam, peace be upon him. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Honor your paternal aunt." It was asked: "And who is our aunt?" He said: "The palm tree."

[[A weak hadith, narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 6/123; Abu Ya'la in his Musnad; Ibn Abi Hatim; Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil: 6/2424; al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa'; and Ibn al-Sunni and Ibn Mardawayh together in al-Tibb. Al-Haythami said: in its chain is Maysarah ibn Sa'id, who is weak. Al-'Uqayli said: its narration is not preserved (ghayr mahfuz). See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/39; Fayd al-Qadir: 2/95; Kashf al-Khafa': 1/195; Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith p. (36); Tanzih al-Shari'ah al-Marfu'ah of Ibn 'Iraq: 1/209. See also on the wisdom of likening faith to the palm tree: Zad al-Masir: 4/359-360.]] ﴿وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ "And Allah sets forth parables for the people, that they may reflect."

[[That is: Allah makes parables for people, and presents to them likenesses, so that they may remember the proof of Allah against them, take heed from it, be admonished, and turn away from the disbelief in which they are, to faith. See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/567.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verse 26:

﴿And the likeness of an evil word﴾ which is shirk (polytheism), ﴿is like an evil tree﴾ which is the bitter gourd (al-handhal), [[Al-Tabari said, 16/585: It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with an authentic report, the statement of the one who said: it is the colocynth (al-hanzalah). If that is authentic, then no other statement may be said. Otherwise, it is a tree with the description God has given it. Then he cited a hadith of al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim from Anas, which Shaykh Mahmud Shakir declared weak. See: al-Tabari: 16/570-571, 585.]]

It is also said: it is garlic (al-thawm).

It is also said: it is the dodder (al-kushuth) [[In "B": al-kushub. In Lisan al-Arab, 2/181: "Al-kushuth, al-akshuth, and al-kushu'i: all of these are a plant that is uprooted and cut at the base. It was said: it has no root, and it is a small plant that clings to the tips of thorns and other things. Al-Jawhari said it is: a plant that clings to the branches of trees without striking its roots into the earth..."]], and it is the ashaqah (ʿashaqah) [[Al-ʿashaqah: a tree that becomes green, then is crushed and turns yellow, and among the later scholars it is the ivy (al-lablab); its plural is al-ʿashaq. See: Lisan al-Arab 10/252.]] ﴿uprooted﴾ meaning it is torn out, ﴿from above the earth, having no stability﴾ meaning no firmness.

Its meaning: it has no firmly established root in the earth, nor a branch rising up to the sky. Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word or righteous deed ascends for him.

The Almighty's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾ refers to the word of monotheism (kalimat al-tawhid), which is the saying: "There is no god but Allah." ﴿In the life of this world﴾ means before death, and ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ means in the grave. This is the view of most of the people of tafsir (exegesis).

It has also been said: "In the life of this world" refers to the questioning in the grave, and "in the Hereafter" refers to the Resurrection.

The first view is the more correct one [[This is the view preferred by al-Tabari, who said (16/602): "The correct interpretation of this matter is what has been established by the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning it, namely that its meaning is: 'Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world,' and that this firmness is His making them firm in this world through faith in Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), 'and in the Hereafter' with the same firmness with which He made them firm in this world, and that is in their graves when they are questioned about the monotheism and the faith in His Messenger (ﷺ) that they held.']].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us: Abu al-Walid related to us: Shu'bah related to us, saying: Alqamah ibn Martad informed me, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn Ubayd, from al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." That is the meaning of the Almighty's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [[Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surah Ibrahim, chapter "Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word": 8/378, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/412.]].

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (Muslim) informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us: Shu'bah related to us with this chain, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾ and said: "It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. It is said to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' That is the Almighty's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾, to the end of the verse [[Related by Muslim in the Book of Paradise and Its Bliss, chapter on the showing of the dead person's seat in Paradise or Hell, no. (2871): 4/220.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Ayyash ibn al-Walid related to us: Abd al-A'la related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), that he related to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he indeed hears the sound of their sandals. Two angels come to him and make him sit up, and they say: 'What did you used to say about this man, Muhammad (ﷺ)?' As for the believer, he says: 'I testify that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.' It is said to him: 'Look at your seat in the Fire; Allah has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise.' So he sees both of them together." Qatadah said: "It was also mentioned to us that his grave is widened for him." Then he returned to the hadith of Anas, saying:

"As for the hypocrite and the disbeliever, it is said to him: 'What did you used to say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know. I used to say what the people say.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, nor did you recite [the guidance].' He is struck with hammers of iron, one blow, and he screams a scream that everyone near him hears, except the two weighty ones (jinn and humans)" [[Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Funerals, chapter on what has been reported about the punishment of the grave: 3/232; Muslim in the Book of Paradise, its bliss and its people, chapter on the showing of the dead person's seat in Paradise or Hell, no. (2870): 4/2200-2201; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/415.]].

Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Isma'il al-Tamimi informed us: Abu al-Qasim Hamzah ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi related to us: Abu Ahmad Abd Allah ibn Adi al-Hafiz informed us: Abd Allah ibn Sa'id related to us: Asad ibn Musa related to us: Anbasah ibn Sa'id ibn Kathir related to us: my grandfather related to me, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The dead person hears the sound of the sandals when the people turn away from him, retreating. Then he is made to sit up, his shroud is placed around his neck, and then he is questioned" [[Related by Ibn Hibban in the Book of Funerals, chapter on the dead person who hears and is questioned, p. (196) of Mawarid al-Zam'an, and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/347, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/413.]].

It is also related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the dead person is buried, two black-blue angels come to him. One of them is called al-Munkar and the other al-Nakir. They say: 'What did you used to say about this man?' He says: 'He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.' They say to him: 'We knew that you would say this.' Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits by seventy, then it is illuminated for him, and it is said: 'Sleep like the sleep of the bride whom none wakes except the dearest of her family to her, until Allah the Exalted raises him.' If he was a hypocrite or a disbeliever, he says: 'I heard the people say something, so I said the same. I do not know.' They say: 'We knew that you would say that.' It is said to the earth: 'Close upon him,' and it closes upon him, so that his ribs interlock, and he continues to be punished in it until Allah raises him from that resting place" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Funerals, chapter on what has been reported about the punishment of the grave: 4/181-184, and he said: "It is a hasan gharib hadith. And on the subject there are reports from Ali, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Abbas, al-Bara' ibn Azib, Abu Ayyub, Anas, Jabir, Aisha, and Abu Sa'id, all of whom narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) about the punishment of the grave." Ibn Hibban also related it in the Book of Funerals, chapter on the dead person being questioned and hearing, p. (197) of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Al-Albani graded it hasan in his commentary on Mishkat al-Masabih and said: "It is according to the condition of Muslim": 1/47.]].

It is related from al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer and said: "Then his soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and make him sit up in his grave, and they say to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? And who is your Prophet?' [He says: 'My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' Then they rebuke him and say to him a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?'] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]] This is the last trial presented to the believer, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic keeps him firm. He says: 'My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out from the heaven: 'He has spoken the truth, My servant.' He said: That is the Almighty's words: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾" [[A portion of a long hadith related by Abu Dawud in the Book of Sunnah, chapter on questioning in the grave: 7/139-141; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/37, 39; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/295-296. Al-Albani graded it sahih in his commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/48. It is also related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir by several routes; see 16/589-595.]]. [194/a]

Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysafuni informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Bistam informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sayyar al-Qurashi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Musa [[In "B": ibn Muhammad.]] al-Farra' Abu Ishaq related to us: Hisham ibn Yusuf related to us: Abd Allah ibn Yahya related to us, from Hani, the client of Uthman, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished burying a man, he would stand over him and say: "Ask forgiveness for your brother, and ask Allah to make him firm, for he is now being questioned" [[Related by Abu Dawud in the Book of Funerals, chapter on asking forgiveness at the grave for the dead: 4/339; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/56; al-Nawawi graded it hasan in al-Adhkar, p. (137); and al-Albani graded it sahih in his commentary on Mishkat al-Masabih: 1/48.]].

Amr ibn al-As said, in the throes of death, while weeping: "When I die, let no mourner accompany me, nor fire. When you bury me, pour the earth over me gently, then stand around my grave for as long as it takes to slaughter a camel and divide its meat, so that I may find comfort in you and consider what answer I should give to the messengers of my Lord."

The Almighty's words: ﴿And Allah leads the wrongdoers astray﴾ mean: He does not guide the polytheists to the right answer in the grave. ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ means: of granting success, abandonment, firmness, and withholding firmness.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 28–30:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude?﴾ and the verse [continues].

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us; Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi related to us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us; al-Humaydi related to us; Sufyan related to us; ʿAmr related to us, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude﴾ [[Omitted in manuscript "b".]], he said: "They are, by Allah, the disbelievers of Quraysh." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surah Ibrahim, chapter: "Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude": 8/378, with the wording: "They are the disbelievers of the people of Makkah." See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/41; al-Tabari: 13/222 (Halabi edition). All subsequent references to the Tafsir of al-Tabari, God willing, will be to this edition, whereas previously we generally cited the Dar al-Ma'arif edition edited by Shaykh Mahmud Shakir.]]

ʿAmr said: "They are Quraysh, and Muhammad ﷺ is the favor of Allah." [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Jarir, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar: 5/42.]]

﴿and caused their people to dwell in the abode of ruin﴾. He said: "The ruin is the Day of Badr." His saying ﴿exchanged the favor of Allah﴾ means: they changed the favor of Allah upon them concerning Muhammad ﷺ, when Allah Exalted sent him from among them, so they disbelieved in him. ﴿And caused [to dwell]﴾, that is: they lodged, ﴿their people﴾ — those who followed them in their disbelief — ﴿in the abode of ruin﴾, that is, destruction. Then He explained the ruin, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 35–36:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾, meaning: the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), ﴿secure﴾, meaning possessing security, in which people are kept safe; ﴿and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols﴾, meaning: distance me (from it). It is said: jannabtuhu al-shay'a, and ajnabtuhu janban, and jannabtuhu tajniban, and ijtanabtuhu ijtinaban, with one and the same meaning.

If it is asked: Abraham, peace be upon him, was already protected (ma'sum) from worshipping idols, so how does the request stand? And many of his sons did worship idols, so where is the answer?

It is said: The supplication on behalf of Abraham, peace be upon him, was for an increase in protection (ismah) and steadfastness. As for his supplication for his sons, he meant his sons from his own loins, and none of them worshipped an idol.

It is also said: his supplication was for those of his sons who were believers [[Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Razi said: "It is said that he asked this request in a state of fear that distracted him from that knowledge (of being protected from disbelief and idol worship), because the prophets, peace be upon them, are the most knowledgeable of people about God, and therefore they are the most fearful of Him, so he is excused for that reason. It is also said: in God's wisdom and knowledge, He does not test any prophet with disbelief, on condition that he be humbly beseeching his Lord and asking Him for that; so He caused this request to flow upon his tongue in order to realize the condition of protection." See: Masa'il al-Razi wa-ajwibatuha min gharib ayat al-tanzil, p. 164.]].

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray﴾, meaning: many have been led astray by them from the path of guidance, to the point that they worshipped them. This is the inverted form (al-maqlub), and its parallel is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175], meaning: he frightens them with his allies.

It is also said: He attributed the leading astray to the idols because they were the cause of it, as one says: "The world has tempted me," attributing the temptation to the world because it is the cause of temptation. [[See also: Masa'il al-Razi wa-ajwibatuha, p. 164.]].

﴿Whoever follows me, he is of me﴾, meaning: of the people of my religion; ﴿and whoever disobeys me, then You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Al-Suddi said: its meaning is: "and whoever disobeys me and then repents."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "and whoever disobeys me in matters short of polytheism."

It is also said: he said this before God informed him that He does not forgive polytheism (shirk). [[In manuscript "b": that one associates with Him.]].

She made a *mintaq* so as to conceal her trail from Sarah. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, brought her and her son Isma'il, while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, at a tree above Zamzam, at the highest point of the mosque. Then Ibrahim turned to leave, and Umm Isma'il followed him and said: "O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no human being and nothing?" She said that to him many times, but he did not turn to her. So she said to him: "Has Allah commanded you to do this?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then He will not neglect us." Then she returned. Ibrahim set off until, when he reached the pass (*thaniyya*), where they could not see him, he faced the House, raised his hands, and supplicated with these supplications, saying: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation﴾, until he reached "they may be grateful."

Umm Isma'il began to nurse Isma'il and drink from that water, until the water in the waterskin ran out. She became thirsty, and her son became thirsty too. She kept looking at him writhing, or, he said, rolling about, and she departed, disliking to look at him. She found al-Safa the nearest mountain to her on the land, so she stood upon it, then faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone. She saw no one. She descended from al-Safa until, when she reached the valley, she lifted the edge of her garment and ran like a distressed person until she had crossed the valley. Then she came to al-Marwa, stood upon it and looked to see whether she could see anyone. She saw no one. She did that seven times.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "For this reason people run between them."

When she came near al-Marwa, she heard a sound and said: "Hush!"—meaning herself. Then she listened and heard it again, and said: "You have made me hear; if you have any help, [then help]." Behold, there was the angel at the place of Zamzam. He scraped with his heel, or he said with his wing, until water appeared. She began to dig into it and say [something] with her hand like this, and she began to scoop water into her waterskin, while it gushed out after she scooped.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on Umm Isma'il! Had she left Zamzam [alone], or he said: had she not scooped from the water, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring."

He said: She drank and nursed her child. The angel said to her: "Do not fear abandonment, for here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build, and Allah does not neglect His people."

The site of the House was raised above the ground like a mound. Floods would come and take away [the earth] from its right and left, and it remained so until a caravan of Jurhum, or a household of Jurhum, passed by them, coming from the way of Kada'. They camped at the lower part of Makkah and saw a bird circling, a bird of augury. They said: "This bird must be circling over water, yet we know this valley has no water in it." So they sent a scout or two, and behold, there was water. They returned and informed them about the water, so they came, while Umm Isma'il was by the water. They said: "Will you permit us to camp with you?" She said: "Yes, but you have no right to the water." They said: "Yes."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: So that pleased Umm Isma'il, for she loved company. They camped and sent for their families, who came and settled with them, until there were households of them there. The boy grew up and learned Arabic from them. He was the most eloquent and admired of them when he grew up. When he reached maturity, they married him to a woman from among them. Umm Isma'il died. Ibrahim came after Isma'il had married, to check on his inheritance [of family]. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *Kitab al-Anbiya'*, chapter on "They hasten in walking": 6/396–398.]] ... We mentioned that story in Surah al-Baqarah. [[See above: 1/147–148.]]

God Almighty said: ﴿Our Lord, so that they may establish prayer, make hearts from among the people incline towards them﴾. *Al-af'idah* is the plural of *al-fu'ad* (heart). ﴿Yearn towards them﴾: they long for them and are drawn to them.

Mujahid said: Had He said "the hearts of people," Persia, Rome, the Turks and India would have crowded you.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Jews, Christians and Magians would have performed Hajj, but He said "hearts from among the people," and they are the Muslims.

﴿And provide for them from the fruits﴾: what You provided for the inhabitants of villages with water, ﴿so that they may be grateful﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 43–44:**

﴿Hastening﴾. Qatadah said: "Hurrying."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Al-ihtada' (the act of hastening) is the nasalan (a swift, gliding run), like the running of a wolf."

Mujahid said: "Constantly gazing."

The meaning of "al-ihtda'" is that they do not turn right or left, and they do not know where their feet are placed.

﴿Raising their heads﴾, that is: lifting their heads.

Al-Qutaybi said: "Al-muqni' (one who raises his head) is the one who lifts his head and directs his gaze toward what is in front of him." [[In Gharib al-Qur'an (1/237), quoting from al-Qartayn by Ibn Mutarrif al-Kinani: "'Al-muqni' ra's hu' is one who raises it and directs his glance toward what is before him. And al-iqna' in prayer means completing it."]]

Al-Hasan said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people's faces will be turned toward the sky, and no one will look at anyone else."

﴿Their gaze will not return to them﴾, that is: their eyes will not come back to them from the intensity of their staring, and they will remain fixed, for what is before them has occupied them.

﴿And their hearts will be emptiness﴾, that is: void. Qatadah said: "Their hearts will have left their chests and come to their throats, neither coming out of their mouths nor returning to their places. So the hearts are empty, with nothing in them. From this, that which lies between the sky and the earth is called hawa' (air/void) because of its emptiness."

It was also said: "Void, not perceiving anything and not understanding anything, from [min, indicating cause] fear."

Al-Akhfash said: "Hollow, with no intellects, and the Arabs call every hollow, empty thing hawa'."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "'And their hearts are hawa'' means: fluttering, churning in their bodies, having no place in which to settle."

The true meaning is that the hearts will be displaced from their places, and the eyes will be fixed from the terror of that day.

﴿And warn mankind﴾, that is: frighten them. ﴿The day﴾, meaning: bi-yawm (with the day), ﴿when the punishment comes to them﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. [195a] ﴿Then those who did wrong﴾, meaning: those who associated partners with God, will say: ﴿"Our Lord, grant us respite﴾, meaning: give us time, ﴿for a short term"﴾. This is their request to be returned to the world, that is: "Send us back to it, ﴿so that we may answer Your call and follow the messengers"﴾. Then they will be answered:

﴿"Did you not swear before, that you would have no decline?"﴾, meaning: you swore in the abode of the world that you would not be removed from it, that is, that you would not be resurrected. This is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that God would not raise up anyone who dies﴾ [al-Nahl: 38].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 45–46:**

﴿And you dwelt﴾ in the world ﴿in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief and disobedience, ﴿the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud and others﴾.

﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾, meaning you knew of Our punishment of them. ﴿And We set forth for you the parables﴾, meaning We made clear that your case is like theirs.

﴿And they had plotted their plot, but their plot was with Allah﴾, meaning the recompense for their plot. ﴿Though their plot was such that﴾ Ali and Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿and in fact their plot was such that﴾ with the letter dal (د), that is, reading وَإِنْ كَادَ مَكْرُهُمْ, while the majority of readers read it with the letter nun (ن), وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ.

﴿Though the mountains would be moved by it﴾. The majority of readers read لِتَزُولَ with a kasra on the first lam and a fatha on the second, i.e., لِتَزُولَ, the second word being in the subjunctive.

Its meaning is: "and their plot was not such that..."

Al-Hasan said: "If their plot were such that the mountains could be moved by it, it would be too weak for that."

It was also said: its meaning is that their plot does not remove the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ), which is as firm as the mountains are firm.

Ibn Jurayj and al-Kisa'i read لَتَزُولُ with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second, i.e., لَتَزُولُ. Its meaning is: even though their plot was great, to the point of reaching a degree that could move mountains, they would not be able to remove the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Qatadah said: its meaning is "and even if their shirk was such that the mountains were about to be moved by it," as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿The mountains are about to fall apart at this, that they ascribe a son to the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 19:90].

It is related from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the meaning of the verse that it was revealed about Nimrod the tyrant, who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord. That is because he said: "If what Ibrahim says is true, I will not stop until I ascend to the sky and see what is there." So he took four young eagles, raised them until they grew up, and made a chest (tabut). He made a door on its top and a door on its bottom. Nimrod sat in the chest with a man, and he set up poles at the corners of the chest and placed meat on their tops, and he tied the chest to the feet of the eagles. The eagles flew up, aiming at the meat, until a day had passed and they had gone far into the air. Then Nimrod said to his companion: "Open the upper door and look at the sky; have we come near it?" He opened [the door and looked], and he said: "The sky is as it was." Then he said: "Open the lower door and look at the earth; how does it appear to you?" He did so, and he said: "I see the earth like a deep sea, and the mountains like smoke." Then the eagles flew for another day and rose until the wind came between them and their flight. He said to his companion: "Open both doors." He opened the upper one, and behold, the sky was as it was; and he opened the lower one, and behold, the earth was black and dark. Then a voice called out: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?"

ʿIkrimah said: There was with him in the chest a boy who had carried with him a bow and arrows. He shot an arrow, and the arrow came back to him smeared with the blood of a fish that had thrown itself from a sea into the air. (It was also said: a bird that the arrow had struck.) Then he said: "I have been relieved of the concern of the god of the sky."

He said: Then Nimrod ordered his companion to level the poles and lower the meat, and he did so. The eagles descended with the chest, and the mountains heard the rustling of the chest and the eagles. They were frightened and thought that some event had occurred from the sky, and that the Hour had come, so they nearly moved from their places. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And though their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾.

[Al-Tabari related this story from Ali and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: 13/244–245. Ibn ʿAtiyyah weakened this story in al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8/265, saying: "There is weakness in this entire story from the standpoint of meaning, since it is impossible for the eagles to ascend as described, and it is unlikely that anyone would endanger himself in such a matter."]

It was also said: its meaning is that their plot does not remove the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ), which is as firm as the mountains are firm.

Ibn Jurayj and al-Kisa'i read لَتَزُولُ with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second, i.e., لَتَزُولُ. Its meaning is: even though their plot was great, to the point of reaching a degree that could move mountains, they would not be able to remove the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Qatadah said: its meaning is "and even if their shirk was such that the mountains were about to be moved by it," as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿The mountains are about to fall apart at this, that they ascribe a son to the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 19:90].

It is related from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the meaning of the verse that it was revealed about Nimrod the tyrant, who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord. That is because he said: "If what Ibrahim says is true, I will not stop until I ascend to the sky and see what is there." So he took four young eagles, raised them until they grew up, and made a chest (tabut). He made a door on its top and a door on its bottom. Nimrod sat in the chest with a man, and he set up poles at the corners of the chest and placed meat on their tops, and he tied the chest to the feet of the eagles. The eagles flew up, aiming at the meat, until a day had passed and they had gone far into the air. Then Nimrod said to his companion: "Open the upper door and look at the sky; have we come near it?" He opened [the door and looked], and he said: "The sky is as it was." Then he said: "Open the lower door and look at the earth; how does it appear to you?" He did so, and he said: "I see the earth like a deep sea, and the mountains like smoke." Then the eagles flew for another day and rose until the wind came between them and their flight. He said to his companion: "Open both doors." He opened the upper one, and behold, the sky was as it was; and he opened the lower one, and behold, the earth was black and dark. ʿIkrimah said: There was with him in the chest a boy who had carried with him a bow and arrows. He shot an arrow, and the arrow came back to him smeared with the blood of a fish that had thrown itself from a sea into the air. (It was also said: a bird that the arrow had struck.) Then he said: "I have been relieved of the concern of the god of the sky."

He said: Then Nimrod ordered his companion to level the poles and lower the meat, and he did so. The eagles descended with the chest, and the mountains heard the rustling of the chest and the eagles. They were frightened and thought that some event had occurred from the sky, and that the Hour had come, so they nearly moved from their places. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 14, verses 47–48:

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir, who said: Abu Hazim ibn Dinar related to me from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white land, pure and smooth, like a loaf of fine bread, with no landmark on it belonging to anyone." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter "Allah Seizes the Earth on the Day of Resurrection": 11/372; and by Muslim in the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on Resurrection and Rising, no. [[Reported by al-Bukhari in the same place: 11/372; and by Muslim in the same place, no. (2792): 4/2151; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/113.]]

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning this verse, that he said: "The earth will be changed into another earth like white, pure silver, in which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed upon it." [[Reported by al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Ba'th" as a marfu' report; and reported as a mawquf report by Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in "al-'Azama," al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th. It was also said: the meaning of the change (tabdil) is making the heavens into gardens and making the earth into fire.

It was also said: the change of the earth is its alteration from one state to another, namely the moving of its mountains, the leveling of its rivers, the smoothing of its valleys, the cutting down of its trees, and making it a level plain (qa'an safsafan). The change of the heavens is the alteration of their condition by the folding up of their sun, the eclipsing of their moon, the scattering of their stars, and their being at one time like red oil (ka-l-dihan) and at another like molten brass (ka-l-muhl).

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Dawud — that is Ibn Abi Hind — from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens as well," so where will people be on that Day, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "On the Sirat (bridge)." [[Reported by Muslim in the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on Resurrection and Rising and the Description of the Earth on the Day of Resurrection, no. (2791): 4/2150. [[A portion of a long hadith, reported by Muslim in al-Hayd, chapter on the description of the semen of man and woman, and that the child is created from their two waters, no. (315): 1/252.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will come forth﴾, that is, they will emerge from their graves, ﴿before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾, who does whatever He wills and decrees whatever He desires.
